summary:
# NOTES: *Elsie's Widowhood* (Martha Finley, 1880, Dodd, Mead & Co.; sequel to *Elsie's Children*)

Preface: author says public demanded Elsie widowhood. Aim: show Christ comforts the bereaved. Epigraph (Holmes): "Alone she wanders where with HIM she trod... she leans on God."

## Key people
- **Elsie Travilla** (née Dinsmore): heroine, widow. Devout; leans on God and father.
- **Edward Travilla** (Mr. Travilla): husband. Dies of sudden illness, Sept., ~age 40s. Earlier daughter **Lily** died young, buried with him.
- **Mr. Horace Dinsmore**: Elsie's father, devoted; becomes guardian/joint executor with Elsie.
- **Rose Dinsmore** ("Grandma Rose"): Horace's wife, Elsie's stepmother.
- **Old Mr. Dinsmore** (grandfather): Elsie's grandfather, aged 80+, moved to Viamede for warm climate. Calls Vi "cricket".
- **Mrs. Louise Conly** (Aunt Louise/Aunt Conly): Roselands; haughty, snobbish. Sons **Calhoun**, **Arthur** (Dr. Arthur Conly), **Walter** (lieutenant, US Army). Daughters **Isadore/Isa**, **Virginia** (proud, scornful, pursues Donald; hates Molly's luck).
- **Children of Elsie & Edward**: **Elsie** (eldest, ~18-19, engaged to Lester), **Edward** (~16, to college; "Ned"), **Violet/Vi** (~15, merry, namesake of mother), **Harold** (tender, becomes doctor), **Herbert** (indolent, "Herbie"), **Rosie** (Rose, ~7-8), **Walter** (4 at father's death).
- **Lester Leland**: Elsie's fiancé, poor sculptor from Fairview; goes to Italy. Engagement announced in Ch II.
- **Molly Percival**: cousin, writer/translator, crippled by fall. Mother **Enna Johnson** (feeble-minded, once proud, now docile). Brother **Dick** (physician). Half-siblings **Bob** and **Betty Johnson** (Oaks).
- **Mr. Embury**: widower of Magnolia Hall; wife Mary died 2 yrs before. Sons **Louis** (eldest) and **Fred**; daughters **Corinna** (5) and **Madie** (3). Called "Mr. February" by Elsie.
- **Isadore/Isa Conly**: marries **Cyril Keith**.
- **Cyril Keith**: young minister, grandson of Cousin Marcia & Stuart Keith (Pleasant Plains, Indiana); son of Cyril Sr.; brother **Donald Keith** (US Army lieutenant). Sister/aunt Mildred mentioned.
- **George Boyd**: nephew of Mrs. Carrington; attempted murder of Travilla; maimed right hand; scarred by **Aunt Dicey's** scalding shower. Starving in New Orleans; dies at Viamede.
- **Mrs. Carrington**: Boyd's aunt, old friend of Elsie and Horace; comes to Viamede.
- **Aunt Chloe**: old mammy/nurse, devoted.
- **Uncle Ben**: old quarter man, cares about Bible truth.
- **Mr. Jones**: young minister, contradicts Scripture (one devil; casting lots wrong); dismissed.
- **Mr. Mason**: former minister at Viamede, transferred away.
- **Miriam Pettit**: leads girls' prayer meeting at Mrs. Mason's cottage.
- **Mr. Will Tallis**: wealthy yachtsman, owner of yacht *Curlew* (Captain Collins). Friend of Edward.
- **Charles (Charlie) Perrine**: Edward's college chum; cousin of Mary Keith; courts Amy.
- **Mary Keith**: Donald's cousin, eldest of 8-9, daughter of Uncle Donald Keith; capable, cheerful; cook.
- **Amy Fletcher**: frail invalid, sweet; Charlie's love.
- **Ella Neff**: teacher, Mary's friend.
- **Mr. & Mrs. William Moses**: Hotel guests at Ocean Beach. William crippled by rheumatism, patient; wife Maria selfish; German servant nurse. Mrs Moses boasts of descent from Moses.
- **Mrs. Perkins**, daughter **Susie**, son **Fred** (19-20): Ocean Beach friends.
- **Ford** (Mr. Ford): widower, courts Elsie in Ch XXV.

## Places
- **Ion**: Elsie's home (Ion, near Roselands/the Oaks). Lakelet, library, nursery, Lily's grave nearby.
- **Roselands**: Conly home, grandfather's residence.
- **The Oaks**: Horace Jr.'s home; Horace Sr.
- **Ashlands** (Carringtons), **Pinegrove** (Howards), **Fairview** (Lelands), **the Laurels** (Mrs. Lacey, Rose's sister).
- **Viamede**: Louisiana (Teche country) plantation, orange groves, lakelet, cottage for minister. Church built by Elsie.
- **Magnolia Hall**: Embury mansion near Viamede, lagoon view.
- **New Orleans**: Boyd encounter; family halts there.
- **Ocean Beach/Long Branch**, NJ: Elsie's summer cottage; Colorado House hotel; Shark River; Manasquan; life-saving station No. --.

## CHAPTER-BY-CHAPTER EVENTS

**Ch I.** Vi finds Elsie crying in mamma's dressing-room; Elsie engaged to Lester Leland; he leaves for Italy in weeks, return in 1-3 yrs. Vi: "no man like papa." Mamma (Elsie): "grace groweth best in winter" (Rutherford quote, papa). Vi tells Elsie to "live like we were kids"; Elsie: "Can't help loving you." Vi tells Molly; Molly sad about own unmarried lot; reflects Christ is her friend.

**Ch II.** Engagement announced by note; family dinner at Ion. Reactions: Mrs. Conly sneers "mesalliance"; Calhoun, Arthur, Isa defend Lester; Virginia "goody-goody". Grandpa Dinsmore is pleased. Isa and Elsie confide. Guest list at dinner (Oaks, Johnsons, Howards, Carringtons, Mrs. Lacey and son, Lelands). Mrs. Conly and Virginia snub Lelands. Lester leaves; Elsie mourns; father's tenderness later regretted.

**Ch III.** September. Edward Travilla, sudden severe pain on return from plantation round. Dr. Arthur Conly, Dr. Barton, city consults. Elsie nurses; Horace, Chloe help. Edward: "Precious little wife" lines; he is dying. Horace tells him truth; Edward: "Is it so, Dinsmore?" Edward blesses children; Elsie consoles ("the Lord... will be our keeper"). Vi and Elsie told by Chloe: "He's mos' dar."

**Ch IV.** Edward's death. Parting words: to Edward "take your father's place"; Harold, Herbert; Walter (4) kisses face; Molly and Enna brought in. Edward buried beside Lily. Elsie faints on threshold; father takes her to rest, won't leave her. Isaiah 43 quoted. Elsie resumes duties after 3 days.

**Ch V.** Children's grief; Rose comforts; Rosie's catechism; Harold "why didn't He let papa stay". Mr. Dinsmore: "I will be a father to you." Children pray. Molly weeps at supper; Enna scolds. Vi visits Molly, quotes Isaiah ("As one whom his mother comforteth"). Elsie visits mother at night; fifth day Elsie returns to breakfast room, empty chair.

**Ch VI.** Ion life; Mr. & Mrs. Dinsmore live at Ion. Will: estate to Elsie for life, then Edward; Elsie & Horace joint executors/guardians. Edward to college. Horace will prepare Harold & Herbert for college. Elsie & Vi talk of Lester; Elsie advises Edward on Bible and infidelity ("study evidences"). Edward asks allowance; Elsie gives it.

**Ch VII.** November, cold. Arthur proposes winter at Viamede for old grandpa's health. Elsie consents (Edward's grave in view). Horace, Rose approve; departure in one week. Molly and Enna invited; Isa invited. Rosie and Walter excited. Elsie breaks down at window; father comforts. Children told; Harold touches mamma's hair.

**Ch VIII.** New Orleans. Horace meets George Boyd (beggar; maimed hand). Boyd flees, caught. Boyd: "Travilla himself can hardly wish me worse." Horace feeds him at restaurant; learns Travilla dead. Gives money for lodging. Horace tells Elsie; she consents to Boyd coming to Viamede (wing room far from family); Mrs. Carrington to be sent for.

**Ch IX.** Elsie writes to Mrs. Carrington. Boyd bathed, clothed, shipped to Viamede. Family arrives Viamede; Elsie's widowed life of service, charity, church giving. Lester writes hopefully. Mamma counsels Elsie to be cheerful. Herbert's Latin lesson: Horace forbids food till recited; mamma tells Herbert her own Latin story ("Grandpa treated me just as he does you"). Mamma: boys must earn living; "Each of my boys must study a profession or learn some handicraft."

**Ch X.** Church built by Elsie; Mr. Mason left; young minister Mr. Jones (candidate). Rosie: "why don't we have a minister that believes the Bible?" Family disputes: Jones said one devil; said casting lots wrong. Evening Bible study on Satan, devils, angels, darkness, chains; Cruden's Concordance. Lessons: armor of God, angels' ministry (Elijah, Lazarus, Daniel, Paul, Peter). Vi and Elsie resolve to serve Jesus fully.

**Ch XI.** Boyd sick, in bed; Elsie avoids him. Horace: Boyd asks Elsie to forgive him. Elsie goes; forgives: "as I hope to be forgiven." Boyd despairs ("the door is shut"; Hebrews/Proverbs passages). Prayers. Boyd dies: "Oh God be merciful to me a sinner!" Mrs. Carrington nearly faints; doubt about salvation. Body sent away, buried with family. Mamma recounts death scene to children; warns, "live not for time, but for eternity." Elsie & Vi studio; Vi painting, Elsie modelling.

**Ch XII.** Sunday talk: Vi and Elsie asked to join Miriam Pettit's girls' prayer meeting in Mrs. Mason's parlor; they agree to pray aloud. Mamma starts women's prayer meeting at Ion. Uncle Ben: doesn't want Jones kept. Mr. Embury (Mrs Embury died 2 yrs ago, two boys away, two girls) visits; opposes Jones; asks to join Bible study. Mrs. Travilla: Jones's errors (no Holy Spirit doctrine, false assurance, doubt). Embury stays to tea; intrigued by Molly. Embury invites family to Magnolia Hall.

**Ch XIII.** Young Cyril Keith preaches (text Jn 15:25 "They hated me without a cause"). Relation revealed: Keith of Pleasant Plains; Horace joy. Elsie's husband's death newly known to him. Cyril stays as preacher to both churches; Embury gives up claim. Isa and Cyril grow close; Embury rival. Molly admires both, thinks they court Isa.

**Ch XIV.** Molly rebellious; refuses drive, feels envy of cousins; Vi and Mr. Embury walk together at croquet, Molly's heart stirs. Elsie consoles Molly, Molly confesses doubts of salvation; Elsie points to Christ. Embury courts Molly; Enna wants match. Elsie fears Molly will be hurt; Embury must stop visits. Aunt Wealthy (nearly 90) cited as happy spinster.

**Ch XV.** Elsie tells father; father hurt by memories of her infancy. Horace to hint to Embury. Isa & Cyril love observed; Aunt Louise will object. Embury absent days; Molly miserable. Embury proposes to Molly in garden; she accepts after protests; he brings daughters Corinna and Madie.

**Ch XVI.** Embury drives Molly to Magnolia Hall; she sees mansion ("you are its mistress"). Horace approves. Dick sent for. Wedding planned in two weeks. Elsie gives Molly $10,000; Embury $50,000 + diamond & pearl jewels. Louis and Fred Embury groomsmen. Wedding at Viamede; Cyril officiates. Isa & Cyril engaged; Elsie offers cottage refurbishing.

**Ch XVII.** Mrs. Conly letters: Isa's consent; Aunt Delaford dowry $25,000 promised. Walter (Lt. US Army) reads Dick's letter. Virginia envy. Molly and Elsie talk of Molly's happiness. Cottage refitted. Isa & Cyril wedding late June; summer at North. Elsie and Vi home at Ion.

**Ch XVIII.** Summer. Edward home; Elsie: "Thank God... my boy has come back... pure." Edward's college. Summer at Long Branch/Ocean Beach cottage. Harold chooses medicine; Herbert indolent; Edward chooses plantation work and agricultural college. Lieutenant Donald Keith visits. Mrs. Conly and Virginia arrive. Edward dislikes Aunt Louise. Edward invites Charlie Perrine.

**Ch XIX.** Vi goes with Edward to Colorado House; Mary Keith meets them; Vi to stay with Mary; Edward and Charlie take rooms on same floor. Hotel: Mr. & Mrs. William Moses (crippled husband, selfish wife); Mrs. Perkins, Susie, Fred. Vi plays and sings hymn "O Jesus, Friend unfailing" to comfort Moses. Mrs. Moses: "Humph, you don't know what trouble is."

**Ch XX.** Mr. Moses's pain; Vi sings to him; sea sunbath; Maria Moses leaves early for NY. Mary's sand box for Moses's hand. Mary: "inasmuch as you have done it unto one of the least."

**Ch XXI.** Mary offers rented cottage (from Mr. Marston) for 2-3 weeks; invites Amy Fletcher and Ella Neff. Vi, Edward, Charlie join. Cottage small; house-warming dinner. Mrs. Dinsmore & Elsie bring hamper; Mary welcomes Dinsmores.

**Ch XXII.** Elsie leaves. Edward and Vi's mother's parting text: "whether ye eat... do all to the glory of God." Household "democracy": Mary cook; Donald chairs; hours set; Mary insists on daily prayer and Bible reading; Edward, Donald, Charlie take turns leading worship. Charlie and Amy's affection noticed. Boating at Shark River.

**Ch XXIII.** Sabbath study; sermon book read; strolls. Elsie visits. Vi cooks dinner for fishing party; disaster (scales left on fish, salt forgotten, pudding heavy). Edward arrives with mamma's hamper ("she will surely fail"). Vi: "screwed my courage to the sticking place." Next day inland walk; wade across inlet; Donald carries Elsie & Vi; life-saving station; life-car and breeches-buoy explained. Charlie carries Amy; Mary's second dinner.

**Ch XXIV.** Yacht *Curlew* of Will Tallis; Edward and Charlie and girls board for voyage to Boston/New Hampshire/Maine. Vi refuses (no mamma consent); Edward goes anyway; Donald stays (Mrs. Perkins invitation). Vi begins saying she'll pray. Storm, lost at sea. Prayers aboard; Amy & Charlie. *Curlew* grounds near Ocean Beach; patrolman's red light; breeches-buoy; life-car rescues Mary, Ella, Amy, Charlie. Edward last; captain last. No lives lost.

**Ch XXV.** Next morning newspaper lists *Curlew* passengers (Tallis, Edward, Charlie, Mary, Amy, Ella). Mamma and grandpa drive to Ocean Beach. Edward thanked; Tallis introduced; Elsie rewards surfmen. Donald remains (flirtation by Virginia rebuffed). Mrs. Conly and Virginia gossip about widowed Elsie and "Mr. Ford" courting her; Mrs. Conly calls Travilla's will "foolish". Vi overhears; in summer-house cries; tells mother. Elsie comforts Vi: "Your beloved father is no more dead to me..." **THE END.**

## Other notes
- Epigraphs use quotes from Holmes, Shelley, Shakespeare, Rutherford, Tennyson, Longfellow, Thomson, Byron, Coleridge, Rogers, others.
- Catalog of other Elsie books at end (Elsie Dinsmore series; Mildred Keith series; Casella; etc.).
